entries.summary_en: The levofloxacin label says blood sugar can swing too low or too high in people on diabetes tablets, so sugar should be checked more often (label example: glyburide, a sulfonylurea like gliclazide).
The ciprofloxacin label warns of low blood sugar, sometimes severe, with diabetes tablets such as sulfonylureas, so sugar should be monitored (gliclazide is a sulfonylurea).
entries.source_section: Ciprofloxacin tablets label, 7 Drug Interactions, Table 11 (Oral antidiabetic drugs); 5.19 Blood Glucose Disturbances

entries.summary_en: The domperidone product information says it must not be taken with medicines that lengthen the heart's QT interval, and it names levofloxacin among such antibiotics.
entries.source_section: Domperidone EU Article 31 referral, Annex III, product information section 4.5 (contraindicated: QTc-prolonging medicinal products, antibiotics e.g. levofloxacin) and 4.3

supporting_sources.section: Levofloxacin label, 5.11 Prolongation of the QT Interval

entries.summary_en: The domperidone product information says caution is needed with azithromycin because both can affect the heart's QT interval.
entries.source_section: Domperidone EU Article 31 referral, Annex III, product information section 4.5 (caution: azithromycin and roxithromycin)

entries.summary_en: Domperidone is not to be used with medicines that lengthen the heart's QT interval, and ondansetron is labelled as one that can do this.
entries.source_section: Domperidone EU Article 31 referral, Annex III, section 4.3/4.5 (contraindicated: QTc-prolonging medicinal products; ondansetron is not named)
